text:
noel.w: Hi folks, quick personal note. I have a diagnosed panic disorder that gets triggered by long all-hands and unexpected live call interruptions. It's been affecting my ability to participate in 90+ minute meetings and Id like to request accommodations: shorter meetings where possible, option to join without video, and written summaries after long sessions. Also would prefer private feedback vs. public callouts during reviews.

jasper.mgr: Thanks for sharing, Noel. I didn't realize this was impacting you. FWIW we rely on longer design deep-dives for context but I'm happy to explore changes. What specific meeting length do you think would help?

noel.w: Shorter is better - 30-45 minute blocks with a clear agenda and a 10-min buffer between meetings helps me reset. For cross-team all-hands, if there's an option for a low-sensory stream (no video, minimal transitions) or a recorded version that's fine too. Written action items after meetings are crucial so I can catch up without rewatching everything.

amira.design: From design side we can split deep-dive sessions into a 30-min presentation + optional open Q&A block. We can also export concise notes afterwards. Happy to pilot this format.

rachel.hr: Thanks for flagging, Noel. This qualifies as a reasonable accommodation. If you're comfortable, please submit the ADA intake form so we have a record; it's not required to start temporary measures. HR can draft an interim accommodation plan while intake and any documentation are pending.

jasper.mgr: I'm supportive of trying a new meeting cadence. My concern is cross-team alignment—some topics require longer discussion. Could we schedule the optional open Q&A after core deliverables, and make sure action owners are listed up-front? Also I'm happy to give feedback 1:1 rather than in public meetings.

noel.w: That sounds great. The 1:1 feedback is really helpful. Also asking to be exempt from mandatory camera-on policies and to have a short "time out" protocol if a panic attack starts (signal via chat to handoff facilitation).

rachel.hr: We'll include those items in the interim plan: meeting length preference (30-45m), camera-optional, written meeting outcomes within 24 hours for large meetings, private feedback default, and a short time-out protocol. I'll draft and post the interim plan here for signatures.

hr-bot: Case created: HR-8472 - "meeting cadence & privacy accommodation (Noel W)". Intake recorded 1847507600. Assigned: rachel.hr.

amira.design: I'll update our recurring meeting invites for next week's deep-dive to follow the split format and add an agenda. We'll mark the Q&A as optional and include a notes doc link.

jasper.mgr: Thanks, team. Noel, I'll also avoid calling on you for live responses and will route questions via chat. Let's try this for 30 days and check in at two weeks.

noel.w: Appreciate the quick response and support. I'll submit the intake today and can provide a brief clinician note if needed. I'll sign the interim plan when it's posted.

rachel.hr: Interim plan draft will be posted by EOD. Confidentiality reminder: details only shared with those on the case. :lock:
